## Purpose and Entry Points
Taste Skill is a content-first repository of portable AI-agent instruction packages for producing higher-quality frontend designs and image-generation references. It is not an application or library runtime. The primary consumer is the external `npx skills add` CLI, which discovers skill definitions beneath `skills/`; users may also copy a skill document directly into an agent context. Repository/plugin metadata is at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

## Skill Package Boundary
Each skill is a self-contained Markdown instruction contract, centered on a `SKILL.md` file with install metadata and agent-facing workflow/design constraints. The external installer selects a package by the frontmatter `name`, rather than necessarily its directory name. Core packages include:
- Default experimental frontend workflow: `skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md`
- Compatibility-preserved v1 workflow: `skills/taste-skill-v1/SKILL.md`
- GPT/Codex-focused stricter variant: `skills/gpt-tasteskill/SKILL.md`

## Frontend Implementation Workflows
Code-producing skills guide an agent from a product brief or existing UI toward implementation, while remaining framework-agnostic. The default skill establishes design-language inference and adjustable variance, motion, and density; specialized variants constrain the target visual language or operating mode:
- Image-reference-to-code pipeline: `skills/image-to-code-skill/SKILL.md`
- Existing-project audit and redesign: `skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md`
- Completion/output enforcement: `skills/output-skill/SKILL.md`

The critical boundary is that skills provide instructions, not executable UI code: the receiving agent and target project own framework choice, code generation, dependencies, and rendering.

## Visual-Direction Variants
Style-specific skill documents layer a defined aesthetic onto an implementation agent’s work: calm premium design, editorial minimalism, or industrial brutalism. These are composable choices rather than application modules:
- `skills/soft-skill/SKILL.md`
- `skills/minimalist-skill/SKILL.md`
- `skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md`

Google Stitch integration is represented as another instruction format; it can optionally produce a design artifact format defined alongside the skill: `skills/stitch-skill/SKILL.md`, `skills/stitch-skill/DESIGN.md`.

## Image-Generation Stage
Image-only skills produce reference boards, web compositions, mobile screen/flow sets, or brand kits. Their output is intended to cross a modality boundary: generated images are subsequently supplied to coding agents, or to the image-to-code workflow, for implementation. Paths:
- `skills/imagegen-frontend-web/SKILL.md`
- `skills/imagegen-frontend-mobile/SKILL.md`
- `skills/brandkit/SKILL.md`

Relevant external runtimes/services are ChatGPT Images or comparable image generators, then Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, or other compatible coding agents.

## Research and Documentation Inputs
The research corpus provides the rationale for anti-repetition and completeness guidance, particularly around model “laziness,” prompt design, parameters, and architectural remediation. It informs skills but is not consumed programmatically:
- `research/laziness/README.md`
- `research/laziness/remediation/architectural-patterns.md`
- `research/laziness/remediation/prompt-engineering.md`

## Publishing Assets and Maintenance
The README is the human-facing catalog and installation guide; assets support repository presentation. Small Node `.mjs` scripts process README/sponsor assets rather than participate in skill execution:
- `README.md`
- `scripts/convert-readme-assets-webp.mjs`
- `scripts/build-emil-sponsor-row.mjs`

There is no indicated deployed service, database, backend, or internal application runtime. The material integration dependency is the Vercel Labs Agent Skills-compatible `npx skills add` discovery/install workflow.
